findings.title: No test for rounding of non-divisible amounts
findings.explanation: The partial-period case uses 3000 over 30 days, so the result is exactly 2000. Real proration usually produces fractional cents, for example 1000 after 10 of 30 days gives 666.67. Add a case that pins down the rounding behavior (round, floor, or ceil) and the return type (integer cents or float). Otherwise a rounding regression would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Degenerate period (end <= start) is not covered
findings.explanation: The PR claims to cover edge cases, but a zero-length or inverted period (start === end, or end before start) is the likeliest cause of a division by zero, NaN or a negative refund. Add a test that documents the expected behavior, such as returning 0 or throwing.

findings.title: 'Partial month' case is not really a partial month
findings.explanation: The description mentions a partial month, but the test uses a full 30-day period (April 1 to May 1) with cancellation 10 days in. The period itself is a whole month. If a real partial month was intended, such as a mid-month start or a 31-day month, add it. Otherwise fix the PR description. A 31-day month would also check that the denominator is derived from the dates and not hard-coded as 30.

findings.title: Multiple assertions per test and duplicated setup
findings.explanation: The start and end dates are repeated in every test, and the boundary tests bundle two scenarios each (exact boundary and beyond it). Splitting these into separate `it` cases, or using `it.each`, with shared `start`/`end` constants would give clearer failure messages. The test title would then show which side of the boundary broke.

findings.title: Time zone and DST sensitivity not exercised
findings.explanation: All dates are UTC midnight, which is fine for these cases. If the implementation uses local-time arithmetic or day counts, a non-midnight cancellation time, or a period crossing a DST change, could behave differently. Consider one test with an intra-day timestamp to document whether proration is by day or by millisecond.
